req.title: Task creation persists
req.statement: The system shall commit new task rows so subsequent GET calls return them across requests.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-021 requires that POST /tasks/ commits new task rows so subsequent GET calls return them. Tests must verify: (1) positive path — a valid POST returns 201 with correct payload and a follow-up GET /tasks/{id} returns the same row; (2) negative path — a POST with an invalid payload (missing required 'title') returns 422; (3) boundary path — a POST with a title of exactly 1 character (min_length boundary) succeeds, and a POST with an empty string title (below min_length) fails. Additional tests cover the title max_length boundary (100 chars vs 101 chars) and the completed boolean invariant (both true and false). All tests use in-process TestClient, exact-value assertions, and only fields that exist in the source schema.

tests.executable:
import os, sys
os.environ.setdefault('DATABASE_URL', 'sqlite://')
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.database import Base, get_db
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

engine = create_engine('sqlite://', connect_args={'check_same_thread': False})
TestingSessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

def override_get_db():
    db = TestingSessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
client = TestClient(app)

def test_post_task_persists_and_get_returns_same_row():
    payload = {'title': 'Integration test task', 'description': 'Verify persistence', 'completed': False}
    r_post = client.post('/tasks/', json=payload)
    assert r_post.status_code == 201
    body = r_post.json()
    assert body['title'] == 'Integration test task'
    assert body['description'] == 'Verify persistence'
    assert body['completed'] == False
    assert isinstance(body['id'], int)
    assert 'created_at' in body
    task_id = body['id']
    r_get = client.get(f'/tasks/{task_id}')
    assert r_get.status_code == 200
    get_body = r_get.json()
    assert get_body['id'] == task_id
    assert get_body['title'] == 'Integration test task'
    assert get_body['description'] == 'Verify persistence'
    assert get_body['completed'] == False

test_post_task_persists_and_get_returns_same_row()

import os
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.database import Base, get_db
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

engine6 = create_engine('sqlite://', connect_args={'check_same_thread': False})
TestingSessionLocal6 = sessionmaker(bind=engine6)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine6)

def override_get_db6():
    db = TestingSessionLocal6()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db6
client6 = TestClient(app)

def test_post_task_appears_in_get_tasks_list():
    r_before = client6.get('/tasks/')
    assert r_before.status_code == 200
    count_before = len(r_before.json())
    r_post = client6.post('/tasks/', json={'title': 'List persistence check', 'completed': False})
    assert r_post.status_code == 201
    new_id = r_post.json()['id']
    r_after = client6.get('/tasks/')
    assert r_after.status_code == 200
    tasks_after = r_after.json()
    assert len(tasks_after) == count_before + 1
    ids_after = [t['id'] for t in tasks_after]
    assert new_id in ids_after

test_post_task_appears_in_get_tasks_list()
